minutes.headline: Building committee aired space-priority ideas for town and school offices; no budget ceiling set and minutes vote failed for lack of members
minutes.summary: The committee discussed a draft position paper on records storage and digitization, then spent most of the meeting on how to prioritize space needs, with members presenting individual "king for a day" scenarios (new office building, reusing Turkey Hill, Ritter for school offices). Members agreed a budget ceiling is needed but disagreed on who should set it. Approval of prior minutes could not proceed for lack of enough eligible voters; the next meeting was planned for June 27.

what_happened.line: Members agreed the town needs a project budget ceiling, but disagreed on who should set it; the Select Board chair will bring it to the Select Board.
Most of the meeting went to ranking space needs for town and school offices, with members offering individual "king for a day" scenarios; no priority was settled.
Members will email their scenarios to the chair, who will compile them and look for what they share at the next meeting.
Approval of prior minutes was deferred because too few eligible members were present to vote; no votes were recorded.
The chair will email a draft records storage and digitization position paper to members and keep it on the next agenda.

why_it_matters: Without an agreed budget ceiling, options for a new office building, reusing Turkey Hill or retrofitting Ritter cannot be priced against what the town can afford, and any resulting project would likely need a town vote to fund it.
Where town and school offices end up, and how records are stored, bears on future capital spending and debt, which are paid mostly through taxes.
watch_next: Next meeting planned for June 27, with the compiled scenarios and the storage position paper on the agenda.
Whether the Select Board takes up a budget ceiling for the project.
